route_note: MultiMarginLoss.cu (buggy 13398dab79 / fix 8573a2beda) copied byte-for-byte (harness/r2_extract.sh; fixdiff.py RESULT PASS, targets/pytorch-3/r2/fixdiff.check). The file is compiled whole: common/driver.cu #includes the verbatim MultiMarginLoss.cu (so the kernel in the anonymous namespace is reachable) and launches MultiMarginLoss_backward_kernel<1,float> exactly as the 1-D-input branch of multi_margin_loss_cuda_backward_out does. The ATen/c10 headers the file includes are the INSTALLED PyTorch 2.14.0+cpu headers (/home/fzheng4/miniconda3/envs/accel/lib/python3.14/site-packages/torch/include, git 08187d9e) used as include shim; the generated header c10/cuda/impl/cuda_cmake_macros.h that a CPU wheel lacks is stubbed (empty) in common/ (ATen/cuda/CUDAConfig.h is stubbed too, same stubs as pytorch-1). Nothing is linked from libtorch: the host functions of the file are compiled but never called and are discarded by -ffunction-sections / --gc-sections at link time. nvcc flags follow PyTorch's CUDA build: -std=c++20 -O3 -DNDEBUG --expt-relaxed-constexpr --expt-extended-lambda -D__CUDA_NO_HALF_OPERATORS__ -D__CUDA_NO_HALF_CONVERSIONS__ -D__CUDA_NO_HALF2_OPERATORS__ -D__CUDA_NO_BFLOAT16_CONVERSIONS__ -DCUB_WRAPPED_NAMESPACE=at_cuda_detail -D_GLIBCXX_USE_CXX11_ABI=1, plus $RW_NVCC_FLAGS (-arch=sm_89) and -lineinfo; never -G. The torch headers are newer than the 2025-07 commit; this only matters for the host code, not the kernel (the kernel text and its SASS come from the verbatim file).
